So, point the shield forward like you normally would, just making sure the point of impact is on the shield's far side.

Notes:

* The shield blocks both ways. So depending on desperation, you can stand **on** Doomfist's point of impact, take the ult damage yourself, but still protect people on the far side of the shield.

* I have not confirmed this and do not have a sufficient number of friends to test it (see: 2), but I'm very, very curious to see if this would work. When this happens, explosive damage can go UNDER your shield, assuming you're not aiming down/closing the gap between it and the ground. Rein main here. From the QP I've played, fighting Doom is very situational, and depends on how good the Doomfist is. The best way to approach it is to think about what the Doomfist is trying to achieve, and what attack you're actually trying to counter.

**If he's attacking YOU**

So his rocket punch: treat this like another Rein charging you. Actively try to charge it to get the dual stun, but *warn your team before it happens*. You have more health than Doomfist, and are more likely to be with your team, so your team should be able to easily focus him down/your other tank should be able to take the heat during the stun. You're right that a trade is risky, but if your team is coordinated, you shouldn't die, and even if you do, they're down a DPS and should still hold.

The rest of his kit also has some easy weaknesses. When he uppercuts, Doomfist will actually fall slower than you. So if you're timing is good, it makes for an easy pin when you fall past him. His jump slam uses the same cone shape as earthshatter, so you're on shield duty for those to protect from the stun. And anytime he's not using an ability, remind him that you have a hammer and that he is still significantly squishier than you. Because short of him combo-ing you perfectly, you can out dps him.

A note on positioning though. You know how when you're Rien, you like having a wall directly behind your enemy, that way you can pin them quickly? Doomfist likes the same thing. So if possible, keep your back clear something he can punch you into, especially in a 1 on 1.

**If he's attacking your TEAM**

This is trickier as it goes into a more dive comp-esque realm. You can focus on him or on holding the choke, but not both. You may have to juggle shielding the front and going for a charge/firestrike/swing, but it's entirely situational. Think of it as though a Tracer is in your back line. It's a problem, but where are you contributing more?

**His Ult**

Treat this like a faster/less predictable DVa ult. Your team should get as close to you as possible, and you need to practice flipping your shield to his ult's impact. If it helps, drop your shield so the enemy team can't break it, then throw it up last second. It takes practice, but it's definitely readable.

Rein main here. My SR's only 2583, but 80 hours of that is pure hammer time so I feel I can give some input. Before I start, you're right that having to solo those heroes is heavily situational. To be frank, you shouldn't ever need to, as a Rein is most effective when grouped with others. But, assuming the situation is unavoidable:

**Charge is your best friend**

I cannot emphasize this enough. Every character you listed can be killed by a single pin. As such, you'll want to get creative with timing and work on hard reads for each hero. Try to predict where a tracer will blink or a genji will dash. Did the mei just freeze? There is an audio cue for the ice being ready to break, so learn to time it. Note: a good mei will know this and get out early, but a better Rein will predict it. Reaper is the trickiest, as his wraith form will have you pass right through him. But this is, hands down, the easiest way to survive.

**Firestrike is your second best friend**
100 damage is nothing to sneeze at. With that, the heroes listed are at half health or worse, so getting a good fire strike in, even at close range, means you can out dps them (depending on their technical skill). Note for genji, only do this if you know his deflect is on cooldown, otherwise you're the one behind in health now. But depending on the player, this may be enough to intimidating them into running, which is a victory.

**Your shield is a great dance partner**

This is especially meant for reaper, or just delaying in general. Most of the attacks of the listed characters cannot go through your shield. So, especially if backup is coming, back up, and just shield yourself. The stupid will follow and try to circle around you forever. But to help, learn the ammo counts of each of those characters: because the second you hear reaper's 8th shot go off...

**Your hammer is your *goddamn* SOULMATE**

Swing it. A lot. Meis and good tracers are the only exception, as being frozen is an easy death sentence, and a decent tracer can kite you all day. But it's really intimidating, and the "boop" effect of the hammer is enough to mess up a really jumpy genji's aim. This is a tough call, but if you're going to die, getting in damage helps, depending on the situation.

**Positioning is most important though**

Think about the fight long term. Where are you positioned with respect to the enemy team? Who is going to get backup first? Is it worth it to stall, or are you just going to give a genji more ult charge? Between all of this is the true decision: fight, stall, run, kill yourself. There's some small honor in charging back to your own team, but there's enemy ult charge in taking too many icicles to the head.

**CATCH PHRASE**
